summary: The v40 replay stops in dog.c:abuse_dog when abuse reduces a leashed pet’s tame value to zero. The C path calls apply.c:m_unleash(mtmp, TRUE), which emits visible or unseen feedback, clears the inventory leash and mleashed state, then lets abuse_dog continue to growl and redraw. The complete helper has 11 existing JavaScript direct-caller branches; three C-only branches remain documented. Banishment also forwards through mon.c:migrate_mon to dog.c:migrate_to_level, so its stale leashed-migration refusal is removed.

source.branch: Port the whole m_unleash helper, including visible/unseen feedback and inventory attachment ordering, and wire every existing JavaScript caller branch at its C source site.

unportedCallSites.reason: No JavaScript check_leash implementation or corresponding call branch exists.
The JavaScript function is partial and currently omits the C tail containing this call; adding only the call would place it before omitted tameness/starvation logic.
The C stay-behind branch is not represented in JavaScript; the existing JavaScript leash-slack branch at the later callsite is wired.

indirectCallers.reason: The existing banishment owner discarded this source path behind a named leashed-migration note; the complete dog migration path now clears both leash attachments before moving the target.

evidence: Saved v40 queue entry (SHA-256 82668c1acaa9af757aba3b94e9829675df7e6a8241f515b0d539f21501e1c5fe) and accepted evaluation challenges/evaluations/accepted-6e5dacedc7638246a629e7fe6295014ecbb0083d-v40.json: 53/55 screens and cursors, 6531/6531 RNG calls, first stop at step 53. Queue case, manifest corpus digest, recipe/recording hashes, and evaluation provenance were rechecked at accepted game commit 6e5dacedc7638246a629e7fe6295014ecbb0083d.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:726-745 defines the complete m_unleash helper: conditional feedback via canseemon/pline_mon or Your, matching leash lookup, leashmon clear and inventory update before the final mleashed clear.
Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/pline.c:138-152 defines pline_mon; js/muse.js had a private messageAt-based helper that will move to the canonical js/pline.js owner.
The triggering source is dog.c:abuse_dog:1362-1396, called from dokick.c:dokick on the admitted v40 kick sequence. It must finish leash cleanup before growl and newsym.

The complete C source inventory has 14 m_unleash call sites. Eleven correspond to existing JavaScript caller branches and are reserved for wiring. The remaining C-only branches are apply.c:check_leash:973, dog.c:mon_catchup_elapsed_time:715, and dog.c:keepdogs:849; each is recorded as unported rather than synthesized.

The saved implementation scope was expanded before edits to reserve artifact.c:invoke_banish and mon.c:migrate_mon. Their JS chain previously skipped a leashed demon after the destination draw; invoke_banish now always uses the existing migration owner, which awaits dog.c:migrate_to_level and apply.c:m_unleash.

additionalEvidence: scripts/artifact-banish.test.mjs verifies a leashed imp follows the C migration and m_unleash path, including destination RNG, leash cleanup and off-map state.
scripts/dogmove-quickmimic.test.mjs and scripts/dogmove.test.mjs verify leashed mimic pets reach the C leashability/release branch; only the steed dismount remains unported.
